correctness.rationale: Deleting occupied sites and their closed neighborhoods gives the unmarked, single-marked and double-marked polynomials C_n+z, z P_{n-3} and z² P_{n-6}; the neighborhoods are disjoint, even at n=7. The constant and linear coefficients of P_{n-6}(C_n+z)-P_{n-3}² are 0 and 1. For n=2m+1 the largest independent-set counts for the two paths and cycle are 1, m and n at degrees m-2, m-1 and m. Hence the covariance tends to (n-m²)/n²<0. In the vacant-hub conditional law the relative pair deficit is q²+O(|q|^{n-4}), with q=−z+O(z²); the rim occupation is z(1+o(1)). The total-covariance identity adds the hub-occupation probability p_n to the negative relative deficit with prefactor (1−p_n) times the squared rim occupation. In the stated window, z e^{nz}=e^s and n z²=o(1), giving C_n∼e^{nz} and p_n/z²→e^{−s}, uniformly for bounded s. A sign bracket at s=±1 gives a zero whose s-coordinate tends to zero by uniform convergence. Since dW(ne^s)/ds=W/(1+W)≤1, its displacement from W(n) also tends to zero. This establishes existence, not uniqueness. The bounded independent replay at n=7,9,11 matched all marked polynomial coefficients and top numerator coefficients −2,−7,−14; the finite profile checks are supplementary.

value.rationale: A natural local occupation pair on a canonical hub-and-rim graph separates two opposing mechanisms: conditional rim repulsion and a shared all-empty-rim event. The explicit normalized profile and additive o(1) location on the n z scale quantify when the latter overtakes the former. This is more informative than finite sign examples or the wheel partition function and gives a useful sharp reference example for covariance sign under graph joins.
